What is Medical Genetics?

Study of biological variation as it pertains to health and disease
Application of genetic principles to medical practice
Study of genes and their effects
Includes inheritance, disease mapping, diagnosis, treatment and genetic counselling

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 8
slides.text:
A brief history of Medical Genetics
 - Mendel, the father of genetics  principles of heredity

 - Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood group system.

 - Johannsen coined the term gene to denote the basic mendelian unit of heredity

 - Oswald Avery showed genes are composed of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
				
 - Watson and Crick discovered the physical structure of DNA.

 - Correct number of chromosomes, 46, finally determined.

 - Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21.

 - The Human Genome Project.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 18
slides.text:
Why do you need to know about Medical Genetics?
Genetic diseases - make up a large percentage of the total disease burden in pediatric and adult populations.

Understanding – If we understand the disease process, it can lead to prevention of the disorder and more effective disease treatment.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 19
slides.text:
Types of Genetic Diseases
Chromosome disorders - entire chromosomes (or large segments of them) are missing, duplicated, or otherwise altered ; E.g.: Down syndrome and Turner syndrome.

Single-gene disorders (mendelian conditions) - single genes are altered; E.g.: cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, and hemophilia.

Multifactorial disorders: result from a combination of multiple genetic and environmental causes ; E.g.: birth defects (cleft lip and cleft palate), adult disorders (diabetes)

Mitochondrial disorders: caused by alterations in the small mitochondrial chromosome.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 23
slides.text:
The Gene
Genes - transmitted from parent to offspring and are considered the basic unit of inheritance
Gene location - located on chromosome on a locus.
Number - Humans are estimated to have 20,000 to 25,000 genes
Composition - Genes are composed of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).





Source: National Human Genome Research Institute.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 24
slides.text:
Composition and Structure of DNA
DNA structure can be considered at three hierarchical levels: 
Primary structure - nucleotide sequence 
Secondary structure - double-stranded helix 
Tertiary structure - higher-order folding that allows DNA to be packed

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 35
slides.text:
Types of Genetic Diseases
Chromosome disorders - Changes in the number or structure of chromosomes.

Single-gene disorders (MONOgenic) - single genes are changed (These are mendelian conditions) 

Multifactorial (Complex) disorders (POLYgenic)- multiple gene combinations changed sometimes with environmental causes.

Mitochondrial disorders - caused by changes in the small cytoplasmic mitochondrial chromosome.

Cytogenetics: The study of chromosomes and their abnormalities

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 36
Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 37
slides.text:
Classification of chromosomal anomalies
Number of chromosomes affected (usually due to error in meiosis)
Aneuploidy - The presence of an abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell.

Polyploidy – The presence of more than one pair of (homologous) chromosomes.

Rearrangement of chromosomes (structural issues ; may be due to error in meiosis or inherited)
Translocations - Unusual rearrangement of chromosomes.   
Deletions -  parts of chromosomes are missing, chromosome deletion syndrome
Duplications -  Chromosome duplication disorders occur due to errors in cell division.
Inversions - An inversion is a chromosome rearrangement in which a segment of a chromosome becomes inverted within its original position.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 38
slides.text:
Single-gene disorders (MONOgenic)
Ahmed Elbediwy
LS5023 –Medical Genetics




Cystic Fibrosis - Affects the lungs and digestive system. 
Sickle Cell Anemia - Causes red blood cells to become misshapen and break down. 
Huntington’s Disease - Leads to the progressive breakdown of nerve cells in the brain. 
Hemophilia A - A disorder that impairs the blood’s ability to clot. 
Tay-Sachs Disease - Affects the nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 39
slides.text:
Cystic Fibrosis

Affects the lungs and digestive system. Caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, leading to thick mucus production.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 40
slides.text:
Sickle Cell Anemia
Causes red blood cells to become sickle-shaped, reducing oxygen delivery and increasing breakdown of cells.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 41
slides.text:
Huntington’s Disease
An inherited neurodegenerative disorder that leads to progressive breakdown of nerve cells in the brain.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 42
slides.text:
Hemophilia A
A blood-clotting disorder caused by deficiency of clotting factor VIII, resulting in prolonged bleeding.

slides.topic: Introduction to Medical Genetics — Genes & Disease Classes — source 43
slides.text:
Tay-Sachs Disease
A rare inherited disorder affecting nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord due to lipid accumulation.
